title: When does mandatory CPD start for Victorian estate agents, and what will it require?
description: Victorian estate agent CPD starts 1 April 2027: five activities a year, two mandatory BLA topics with a written exam, eligible providers and records.
shortAnswer: Mandatory continuing professional development (CPD) for Victorian estate agents and agents' representatives starts on 1 April 2027 under section 37K of the Estate Agents Act 1980 and the Estate Agents (Education) Amendment Regulations 2026. Each year from 1 April to 31 March, they must complete at least five CPD activities of at least one hour from an eligible provider, including at least two mandatory activities set by the Business Licensing Authority with a written examination.
keyTakeaways: The first CPD year for estate agents and agents' representatives runs from 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028. The amending regulations (S.R. No. 51/2026) come into operation on 25 November 2026.
Each activity must last at least one hour, be delivered in person or in a live interactive online format, and have consumer outcomes or regulatory compliance as a primary learning objective.
Self-led study, conferences, discussion groups and pre-recorded webinars do not count.

At least two of the five activities must be mandatory activities approved by the Business Licensing Authority (BLA) and must end in a written examination. Eight mandatory activities are listed for 2027-28.
The prescribed record is a certificate for each activity naming the activity, the agent, the provider and the date, with the provider's certification that it is genuine.
jurisdiction: Australia (Victoria): Estate Agents Act 1980 and Estate Agents (Education) Regulations 2020, as amended by the Estate Agents (Education) Amendment Regulations 2026
regulator: Business Licensing Authority (BLA), supported by Consumer Affairs Victoria
appliesTo: Licensed estate agents, including officers in effective control of agencies
Agents' representatives, who must be registered with the BLA from 25 November 2026
Agencies that employ agents' representatives and schedule their training
Registered training organizations and prescribed bodies that deliver CPD activities

sections.heading: Is CPD mandatory for Victorian estate agents yet?

blocks.text: Not yet. As at November 2026, the legal framework has been made but the first CPD year has not begun. Consumer Affairs Victoria's [CPD page](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/licensing-and-registration/cpd-for-property-professionals/continuing-professional-development-for-property-professionals) (last updated 19 October 2026) sets the first CPD year for estate agents and agents' representatives as 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028. Conveyancers start on the same date, and owners corporation managers a year later, on 1 April 2028.

items: 26 May 2026: the Estate Agents (Education) Amendment Regulations 2026 are made.

25 November 2026: the amending regulations come into operation, and agents' representatives must hold a BLA registration (existing representatives on the BLA register on 24 November 2026 are registered automatically).
1 April 2027: the CPD obligation, provider notification duties and record requirements apply.
31 March 2028: end of the first CPD year.

blocks.text: The obligation comes from amendments to the Estate Agents Act 1980. The amending regulations state that they prescribe CPD requirements for the purposes of section 37K(1), and records for the purposes of section 37K(2), of that Act.

sections.heading: What counts as a CPD activity in Victoria?

blocks.text: An activity counts only if it meets all of the content and delivery conditions in regulation 11(1), inserted by the [Estate Agents (Education) Amendment Regulations 2026](https://www.legislation.vic.gov.au/as-made/statutory-rules/estate-agents-education-amendment-regulations-2026). Those conditions are deliberately narrower than many voluntary industry CPD schemes.

items: Delivered directly by a CPD provider, either in person or online in a format that requires the person to interact with the content while it is being delivered.
Not self-led private study, and not a conference or discussion group.
Relevant to an estate agent's or agent's representative's occupation.
Has as a primary learning objective the development of skills or knowledge that improve outcomes for consumers, or compliance with legislative or regulatory requirements.

blocks.title: Primary text: Regulation 11(1)(a), example
blocks.text: "Watching a pre-recorded seminar online does not involve interaction or engagement with the activity while it is being delivered."

The BLA can also determine in writing that a specific activity does not comply with regulation 11(1). Under regulation 10(2), an activity covered by such a determination, or delivered by a provider under a prohibition notice, does not count toward the five.

sections.heading: What are the mandatory CPD activities for 2027-28?

blocks.text: At least two of each person's five activities must be mandatory activities approved by the BLA under section 37M(1) of the Act, and each must require a written examination that evaluates the person's learning (regulation 11(2)). Consumer Affairs Victoria lists eight mandatory activities for 2027-28:

blocks.caption: BLA mandatory CPD activities for estate agents and agents' representatives, 2027-28 (as published by Consumer Affairs Victoria, as at November 2026)
head: Mandatory activity
Most relevant to
rows: Legislative & Regulatory Compliance: Residential Real Estate Property Management
Legislative & Regulatory Compliance: Residential Real Estate Sales
Legislative & Regulatory Compliance: Commercial Real Estate, Repair and Maintenance provisions of Retail Leases
Legislative & Regulatory Compliance: Commercial Real Estate, Rent Reviews and Valuations for Retail Leases
Legislative & Regulatory Compliance: Commercial Real Estate, Assignment of Retail Leases
Licensees and staff handling trust money

blocks.text: The "most relevant to" column is an editorial suggestion, not part of the BLA list. The regulations require two mandatory activities but do not tie particular topics to particular roles, so an agency can choose the two that best fit each person's work.

sections.heading: Who can deliver CPD to Victorian estate agents?

blocks.text: Only an eligible CPD provider can deliver activities that count. Under the new regulation 5 definition, that means a registered training organization approved by ASQA or the VRQA to deliver CPP41419 Certificate IV in Real Estate Practice or CPP51122 Diploma of Property (Agency Management) in Victoria, an organization listed in new Schedule 5, or a person contracted by or acting as agent for either.

Schedule 5 lists five organizations: The Real Estate Institute of Victoria Limited, Australian Livestock & Property Agents Association Limited, Real Estate Buyers Agents Association Incorporated, Australian Institute of Business Brokers Limited, and Tenants Victoria Ltd. From 1 April 2027, providers must notify the BLA before offering an activity, including a course outline for each activity, and must notify changes to outlines or to their RTO status (regulation 13). Consumer Affairs Victoria's [provider page](https://www.consumer.vic.gov.au/licensing-and-registration/cpd-for-property-professionals/become-a-cpd-provider) sets out the notification form.
The BLA can prohibit a provider that delivers non-compliant activities or fails to notify, for up to 3 years, with at least 7 days' notice before the prohibition takes effect (regulation 16).

sections.heading: What records should Victorian agencies keep for CPD?

blocks.text: Regulation 12 makes the certificate the prescribed record. From 1 April 2027 it must show the title of the activity, the name of the agent or representative, the provider's name, the date or dates undertaken, and the provider's certification that the certificate is genuine. The table below maps the obligations to evidence; it is an illustrative template, not a BLA form.

blocks.text: Agencies with offices in both states should note how this differs from [NSW real estate CPD](/regulations/nsw-real-estate-cpd-requirements), which uses hours by area of practice and a 1 July year. For building the schedule, see [how to set mandatory training refresh cycles](/guides/how-to-set-mandatory-training-refresh-cycles) and [how to prepare training records for an audit](/guides/how-to-prepare-training-records-for-an-audit).

sections.heading: How does Knowledge Foundry approach this?

blocks.text: Knowledge Foundry can map each BLA mandatory activity to the specific agency procedures it touches, such as trust account reconciliation or privacy incident handling, so that the written examination and internal assessment test the same outcomes. That gives a principal evidence of in-house competence alongside the provider certificates. See [professional services](/industries/professional-services).

faqs.q: Do conferences count toward Victorian estate agent CPD?
faqs.a: No. Regulation 11(1)(b) excludes conferences and discussion groups, as well as self-led private study. Consumer Affairs Victoria also states that pre-recorded webinars do not count. An activity must be delivered live by an eligible provider, in person or in an interactive online format, and last at least an hour.

faqs.q: Do agents' representatives in Victoria have to complete CPD?
faqs.a: Yes. From 1 April 2027, registered agents' representatives have the same obligation as licensed estate agents: at least five compliant activities each year, two of them BLA mandatory activities with a written examination. Agents' representatives must be registered with the BLA from 25 November 2026.

faqs.q: Can CPD completed before April 2027 count in Victoria?
faqs.a: The obligation in regulation 10 applies on and from 1 April 2027 to each 12-month period from 1 April to 31 March, so the first counting period is 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028. Training completed before then supports competence but does not fall within the first CPD year.

faqs.q: Can an industry body that is not an RTO deliver Victorian CPD?
faqs.a: Only if it is one of the five organizations in Schedule 5, such as the Real Estate Institute of Victoria, or is contracted by or acts as agent for an eligible RTO or Schedule 5 organization. Other bodies cannot deliver activities that count.

sources.title: Continuing professional development for property professionals
New rules: Estate agents and agents' representatives
Estate Agents (Education) Amendment Regulations 2026, S.R. No. 51/2026 (as made)

factCheck.claim: First CPD year for estate agents and agents' representatives is 1 April 2027 to 31 March 2028; conveyancers same; owners corporation managers from 1 April 2028; at least 5 activities, each at least 1 hour, in person or interactive online, from provider list; at least 2 BLA mandatory activities with written assessment; conferences, self-study and pre-recorded webinars do not count; eight mandatory activities listed for 2027-28.

S.R. No. 51/2026 made 26 May 2026, in operation 25 November 2026; prescribes CPD for section 37K(1) and records for section 37K(2) of the Estate Agents Act 1980; regulation 10 requires at least 5 activities each 1 April to 31 March period from 1 April 2027.

Regulation 11(1) content conditions (direct delivery, no self-led study or conference, at least one hour, relevance, consumer outcomes or compliance objective); regulation 11(2) two mandatory activities approved under section 37M(1) with written examination; regulation 12 certificate contents; regulation 13 provider notices; regulation 16 prohibition up to 3 years with at least 7 days notice; Schedule 5 lists five organisations.

Agents' representatives must hold a registration from 25 November 2026; existing representatives on the BLA register on 24 November 2026 automatically registered; CPD from 1 April 2027 for licensed agents and representatives.

Eligible providers: RTOs approved by ASQA or VRQA to deliver CPP41419 or CPP51122 in Victoria, the five prescribed organisations, and their contractors or agents; providers must notify the BLA before offering activities.
